technical_and_design_decisions: All new modules (JDBC source, Redis sink, Kafka sink) will adhere to existing Spring XD module scaffolding, lifecycle, and configuration patterns to ensure consistency with the current codebase and reduce development overhead.

The extendable Trigger abstraction (U4) will use a public interface-based extension point, leveraging Spring's dependency injection to load custom trigger implementations without requiring modifications to core framework code.

ZooKeeper node security (U3) will be implemented by integrating Spring Security with native ZooKeeper ACLs, reusing existing Spring XD ZooKeeper client utilities for connectivity and node operations to avoid redundant work.

HTTPS enablement for the Admin server (U8) will leverage Spring Boot's built-in embedded Tomcat SSL configuration capabilities, with all SSL-related properties exposed as user-configurable options in the Spring XD configuration.

The custom module guidance example (U5) will be a minimal custom source module that emits a static test message, designed to demonstrate all required steps for module development, packaging, and deployment without unnecessary complexity.
The e2e test socket hang up fix (U7) will prioritize process management and configuration adjustments over architectural changes to minimize risk to existing server and test functionality.
assumptions: All required third-party dependencies (Spring Integration JDBC, Spring Data Redis, Spring for Apache Kafka, Spring Boot 1.1.7 SNAPSHOT) are available in public Maven repositories and are fully compatible with the existing Spring XD 1.1.x codebase.
Existing Spring XD build scripts, test utilities, module templates, and CI/CD pipelines are available for reuse, eliminating the need to build custom development and testing infrastructure.
Test instances of Apache ZooKeeper, Redis, and Apache Kafka are available and accessible for integration testing of the respective security, source, and sink features.

The root cause of the Grunt Protractor 'Fatal error: socket hang up' (U7) is a process port conflict or event loop limitation that can be resolved with configuration or process management changes, rather than requiring a rewrite of the test or server infrastructure.
The custom module guidance (U5) does not require complex business logic, only a minimal working example to demonstrate the recommended development pattern for Spring XD modules.

No major breaking changes to existing Spring XD public APIs or module contracts are required to implement the requested features, minimizing the need for extensive regression testing of existing functionality.

activities.activity_description: Implement the native JDBC source module per U1, including configuration properties for database connection, polling interval, and custom query; implement data ingestion logic with error handling and retry mechanisms; integrate with Spring XD module lifecycle; and write unit and basic integration tests against a test database.

Implement the Redis sink module per U2, including configuration for Redis connection, data serialization format, and target Redis key/collection; implement message publishing logic with error handling; integrate with Spring XD sink lifecycle; and write unit and integration tests against a test Redis instance.

Implement ZooKeeper node security per U3, integrating Spring Security with native ZK ACLs; add user/application access control configuration options; implement access restriction logic for zNode read/write/delete operations; and test with multiple permission and authentication scenarios.

Refactor the existing Trigger abstraction to be extensible per U4, define a public extension point interface for custom trigger implementations; update core trigger loading, initialization, and execution logic to support custom implementations; add documentation for custom trigger development; and write unit tests for the extension functionality.

Implement the Kafka sink module per U6, including configuration for Kafka broker connection, message serialization format, and target topic; implement high-throughput message publishing logic with error handling and offset management; integrate with Spring XD sink lifecycle; and write unit and integration tests against a test Kafka instance.
